question: Bramho Samaj was founded by whom?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raja Ram Mohan Roy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha (later renamed Brahmo Samaj) in 1828 in Calcutta. (ब्रह्म समाज — राजा राम मोहन राय)

 

• It was one of the earliest and most influential socio-religious reform movements of colonial India, opposing idol worship, sati and caste rigidity, and advocating monotheism based on the Upanishads.

 

• Ram Mohan Roy is widely regarded as the "Father of Modern India" / "Father of the Indian Renaissance" for his pioneering reform work in religion, society and education.

 

• He also founded the Atmiya Sabha (1815), a precursor to the Brahmo Sabha, and campaigned for the abolition of Sati.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• After Ram Mohan Roy's death, Debendranath Tagore reorganised and strengthened the Brahmo Samaj from 1843 onwards.

 

• Ram Mohan Roy's efforts led to the Bengal Sati Regulation, 1829, banning the practice of sati, under Governor-General Lord William Bentinck.

 

NOTE

 

• Keshab Chandra Sen (Option 2): He led a breakaway faction called the Brahmo Samaj of India (1866), splitting from Debendranath Tagore's Adi Brahmo Samaj.

 

• Debendranath Tagore (Option 3): He joined and revitalised the Brahmo Samaj after Ram Mohan Roy's death; he was the father of Rabindranath Tagore.

 

• Dayanand Saraswati (Option 4): He founded the Arya Samaj in 1875, a separate Hindu reform movement based on Vedic teachings.

question: Who among the following, along with her close associates, started the secret congress radio during the Quit India Movement?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Usha Mehta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Usha Mehta, along with close associates, started the underground Secret Congress Radio in 1942 during the Quit India Movement. (गुप्त कांग्रेस रेडियो — उषा मेहता)

 

• The radio station broadcast messages from national leaders and updates on the movement clandestinely from Bombay, evading British detection for several months before being tracked down.

 

• She was arrested in November 1942 and imprisoned until 1946; she was later honoured with the Padma Vibhushan in 1998.

 

• The Congress Radio operated at 42.34 metres wavelength and was supported by figures such as Ram Manohar Lohia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on 8 August 1942 at the Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, with the call "Do or Die".

 

• Usha Mehta is also remembered for her lifelong involvement in the Gandhian constructive programme after independence.

 

NOTE

 

• Bhikaiji Cama (Option 1): A revolutionary who unfurled an early version of the Indian national flag at the International Socialist Congress in Stuttgart, Germany, in 1907.

 

• Lakshmi Sehgal (Option 2): Associated with the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj); she headed its all-women Rani of Jhansi Regiment.

 

• Sarojini Naidu (Option 3): Known as the "Nightingale of India"; she was the first woman President of the Indian National Congress (1925) and later Governor of the United Provinces.

question: Which Kushana ruler was famous in history as a great patron of Buddhism and organised the fourth Buddhist Council?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kanishka.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kanishka, the most famous ruler of the Kushana dynasty, was a great patron of Buddhism and organised the Fourth Buddhist Council at Kundalvana in Kashmir. (कुषाण शासक, चतुर्थ बौद्ध संगीति — कनिष्क)

 

• The council was presided over by Vasumitra, with Ashvaghosha as vice-president, and it is here that Buddhism formally split into Mahayana and Hinayana sects.

 

• Kanishka started the Saka Era in 78 CE, which is still used as the Indian national calendar.

 

• He patronised Gandhara and Mathura schools of art, and famous scholars such as Ashvaghosha, Nagarjuna, Vasumitra and Charaka adorned his court.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kanishka's capital was Purushapura (modern Peshawar), where he built a famous stupa.

 

• The Third Buddhist Council was held under Ashoka at Pataliputra, presided over by Moggaliputta Tissa.

 

NOTE

 

• Vasudeva I (Option 1): The last great Kushana ruler; the Kushana empire began to decline after his reign.

 

• Vima Kadphises (Option 2): Kanishka's predecessor; he issued gold coins and was a worshipper of Shiva.

 

• Huvishka (Option 4): Kanishka's successor, who built the town of Hushkapura in Kashmir.

question: Akham Lakshmi Devi, a recipient of the Sangeet Natak Akademi award, is renowned for which of the following dances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipuri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Akham Lakshmi Devi is a noted exponent and guru of Manipuri dance, recognised with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for her contribution to this classical dance form. (मणिपुरी नृत्य — अखम लक्ष्मी देवी)

 

• Manipuri is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, originating in the state of Manipur in Northeast India.

 

• It is characterised by graceful, fluid movements, devotional (Vaishnavite) themes, and the absence of ankle bells, unlike most other classical forms.

 

• The Raas Leela is one of the most celebrated repertoires of Manipuri dance, depicting the life of Radha and Krishna.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Guru Bipin Singh is credited with reviving and popularising Manipuri dance across India in the 20th century.

 

• The Jhaveri Sisters are also well-known exponents of Manipuri dance, trained under Guru Bipin Singh.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathak (Option 1): A classical dance form of North India, associated with storytelling through rhythmic footwork and spins; exponents include Birju Maharaj.

 

• Odissi (Option 2): A classical dance form of Odisha, characterised by tribhangi (three-bend) postures.

 

• Sattriya (Option 3): A classical dance form of Assam, originating in the Vaishnavite monasteries (sattras) established by Srimanta Sankardev.

question: Why can you not see objects in a dim lit room when you come from a brightly lit room?
option_1: The iris dilates the eye lens to allow less light to enter the eye.
option_2: The iris contracts the pupil to allow less light to enter the eye.
option_3: The vitreous humour dilates the pupil to allow less light to enter the eye.
option_4: The cornea contracts the pupil to allow less light to enter the eye.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The iris contracts the pupil to allow less light to enter the eye.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The iris is the coloured, muscular diaphragm of the eye that controls the size of the pupil, regulating the amount of light entering the eye. (परितारिका — पुतली का संकुचन)

 

• In bright light, the iris contracts the pupil (makes it smaller) to prevent excess light from entering and damaging the retina.

 

• When you suddenly move into a dim room, the pupil is still constricted from the bright light and takes a short time to dilate (widen) again; until it does, insufficient light reaches the retina, so you temporarily cannot see clearly.

 

• This adjustment process is called dark adaptation and typically takes a few seconds to minutes to complete.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The retina contains photoreceptor cells — rods (sensitive to dim light) and cones (sensitive to bright light and colour); rods take longer to adapt, which is why full dark adaptation is gradual.

 

• The lens, not the iris, is responsible for focusing light on the retina by changing its curvature (accommodation).

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 is incorrect: The iris controls the pupil, not the eye lens; the iris does not "dilate the lens".

 

• Option 3 is incorrect: The vitreous humour is the transparent gel filling the eyeball behind the lens; it does not control pupil size.

 

• Option 4 is incorrect: The cornea is the transparent front covering of the eye that refracts light; it does not contract the pupil — that is the iris's function.

question: Guru Bipin Singh is associated with which of these dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Manipuri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Guru Bipin Singh was a legendary dancer, choreographer and guru credited with reviving and popularising Manipuri dance across India in the 20th century. (मणिपुरी नृत्य — गुरु बिपिन सिंह)

 

• He trained many disciples, most notably the Jhaveri Sisters (Nayana, Suverna, Ranjana and Darshana Jhaveri), who carried forward his legacy.

 

• He established the Manipuri Nartanalaya to teach and propagate this classical dance form.

 

• He was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for his contribution to Manipuri dance.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Manipuri dance draws heavily on Vaishnavite themes, especially the Raas Leela depicting Radha-Krishna devotion.

 

• Other noted Manipuri dance gurus/exponents include Akham Lakshmi Devi.

 

NOTE

 

• Kathak (Option 1): North Indian classical dance form; noted exponents include Birju Maharaj.

 

• Odissi (Option 2): Classical dance of Odisha; noted exponents include Kelucharan Mohapatra.

 

• Kathakali (Option 4): Classical dance-drama of Kerala known for elaborate costumes and facial makeup.

question: Which of the following is the correct duration of ‘Financial Year 2022-23’ in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2023.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In India, the Financial Year (FY), also called the fiscal year, runs from 1 April to 31 March of the following calendar year. (वित्तीय वर्ष — 1 अप्रैल से 31 मार्च)

 

• Accordingly, Financial Year 2022-23 spans from 1 April 2022 to 31 March 2023.

 

• The Union Budget of India is also presented for this same April-to-March financial year cycle.

 

• This practice dates back to British colonial administration and continues to be followed by the Government of India, most state governments, and most Indian companies.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A committee headed by Dr. Shankar Acharya in 2016-17 examined the possibility of shifting India's financial year to a January-December cycle but the change was not implemented.

 

• The Assessment Year (AY) under Indian income tax law is the year immediately following the financial year, in which income of the FY is assessed.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 are incorrect as they do not reflect India's standard 1 April to 31 March financial year cycle.

question: Which of the following pairs of countries are going to host 2022 FIVA Volleyball Women’s World Championship?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Poland and Netherlands.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2022 FIVB Volleyball Women's World Championship was jointly hosted by Poland and the Netherlands, held from 23 September to 15 October 2022. (फीवा महिला विश्व चैंपियनशिप 2022 — पोलैंड और नीदरलैंड)

 

• The tournament was organised by the FIVB (Fédération Internationale de Volleyball), the sport's international governing body.

 

• The United States won the tournament, defeating Brazil in the final to claim their first Women's World Championship title.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2022 edition was the 19th edition of the FIVB Volleyball Women's World Championship.

 

• The men's counterpart, the 2022 FIVB Volleyball Men's World Championship, was held in Russia (originally) before being moved and eventually hosted by Poland and Slovenia due to Russia's suspension over the Ukraine invasion.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 are incorrect as none of these country pairs (Poland-Slovenia, Belarus-Slovenia, Lithuania-Poland) hosted the 2022 FIVB Women's World Championship; Poland and Slovenia in fact co-hosted the men's edition that year.

question: According to traditional Indian seasons (Ritus), which of the following seasons falls in the months of November-December? (Translated from the original Hindi: "पारंपरिक भारतीय ऋतुओं के अनुसार, निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी ऋतु नवम्बर-दिसम्बर के महीनों में आती है?")
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hemant.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the traditional Indian six-season (Ritu) calendar, Hemant Ritu (early winter) falls approximately from mid-November to mid-January, i.e., broadly the months of November-December. (हेमंत ऋतु — नवंबर-दिसंबर)

 

• The traditional six Ritus in order are: Vasant (spring, mid-March–mid-May), Grishma (summer, mid-May–mid-July), Varsha (monsoon, mid-July–mid-September), Sharad (autumn, mid-September–mid-November), Hemant (early winter, mid-November–mid-January) and Shishir (late winter, mid-January–mid-March).

 

• This classification is rooted in ancient Indian texts and the Hindu lunar calendar, where each Ritu spans roughly two lunar months.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The six Ritus together complete one full year in the traditional Indian calendar and are frequently referenced in classical Sanskrit literature, including Kalidasa's Ritusamhara.

 

NOTE

 

• Sharad (Option 1): Corresponds to autumn, roughly mid-September to mid-November, immediately preceding Hemant.

 

• Shishir (Option 2): Corresponds to late winter, roughly mid-January to mid-March, following Hemant.

 

• Vasant (Option 4): Corresponds to spring, roughly mid-March to mid-May.

question: According to World Bank, what was the density of the population of Sri Lanka in 2020?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 354 Persons per sq. km.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per World Bank data, Sri Lanka's population density in 2020 was approximately 354 persons per sq. km. (जनसंख्या घनत्व — श्रीलंका)

 

• Sri Lanka is an island nation in South Asia with a land area of about 65,610 sq. km. and a population of roughly 21-22 million in 2020.

 

• Population density is calculated as the total population divided by the land area, expressed as persons per square kilometre.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's population density (World Bank, around the same period) is significantly higher, at roughly 420-480 persons per sq. km.

 

• Sri Lanka's capital (administrative) is Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte, while Colombo is its largest city and commercial capital; its currency is the Sri Lankan Rupee.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 (554, 300 and 364 persons per sq. km.) are incorrect as they do not match the World Bank's recorded figure of approximately 354 persons per sq. km. for Sri Lanka in 2020.

question: Which of the following is found in plant cells only?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cell wall.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The cell wall is a rigid, non-living outer layer, mainly composed of cellulose, found exclusively in plant cells (also in fungi, algae and bacteria, but not in animal cells). (कोशिका भित्ति — केवल पादप कोशिका)

 

• It provides mechanical strength, shape, and protection to the plant cell, and helps in preventing excessive water uptake.

 

• In contrast, animal cells lack a cell wall and are bound only by a flexible cell membrane (plasma membrane).

 

• The cell wall lies external to the cell membrane in plant cells.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Plant cell walls typically have three layers: the middle lamella, primary wall, and (in mature cells) a secondary wall.

 

• Other structures unique to plant cells include the large central vacuole and chloroplasts (in photosynthetic cells).

 

NOTE

 

• Cell membrane (Option 1): Present in both plant and animal cells; it is the selectively permeable boundary of the cell.

 

• Nucleolus (Option 3): Present in both plant and animal cells; it is involved in ribosome synthesis within the nucleus.

 

• Mitochondria (Option 4): Present in both plant and animal cells; it is the site of cellular respiration and ATP production.

question: Which Mughal ruler contributed to the revolt of 1857?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bahadur shah II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bahadur Shah II (Bahadur Shah Zafar), the last Mughal emperor, was declared the symbolic leader/Emperor of India by the rebelling sepoys during the Revolt of 1857. (1857 का विद्रोह — बहादुर शाह द्वितीय)

 

• Although he had little real political power at the time (British controlled Delhi administratively), his acceptance of leadership gave the revolt a unifying symbol and legitimacy across northern India.

 

• After the revolt was suppressed, he was tried by the British, exiled to Rangoon (Yangon), Burma, where he died in 1862, marking the formal end of the Mughal dynasty.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Key leaders of the 1857 revolt included Rani Lakshmibai (Jhansi), Nana Sahib (Kanpur), Tantia Tope, Begum Hazrat Mahal (Awadh), and Kunwar Singh (Bihar).

 

• The revolt of 1857 is also referred to as India's First War of Independence by many historians, including V.D. Savarkar.

 

NOTE

 

• Shahalam II (Option 1): Mughal emperor during the late 18th century, associated with the Battle of Buxar (1764) and the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), granting Diwani rights to the East India Company.

 

• Bahadur shah I (Option 2): Mughal emperor (r. 1707-1712), son and successor of Aurangzeb.

 

• Alamgir II (Option 3): Mughal emperor (r. 1754-1759), largely a puppet ruler controlled by his wazir Imad-ul-Mulk.

question: Which of the following states presented the ‘Child Budget’ for the first time in March 2022 as a part of their annual financial plan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Madhya Pradesh became the first Indian state to present a dedicated "Child Budget" as part of its annual state budget, in March 2022. (चाइल्ड बजट — मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• The Child Budget is a statement outlining the allocations made across various departments specifically for the welfare, health, nutrition, education and protection of children.

 

• This initiative was aimed at ensuring transparent tracking of expenditure directed towards child development in the state.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Madhya Pradesh has similarly presented a separate "Gender Budget" in its state budgets to track expenditure benefiting women.

 

• The Union Budget of India also includes a "Gender Budget Statement" at the national level, though a dedicated national Child Budget has not been a standard feature.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 (Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Arunachal Pradesh) are incorrect as none of these states were the first to present a Child Budget in March 2022; that distinction belongs to Madhya Pradesh.

question: Which of the following perennial rivers is 720 km long and originates in the Himalayas in flow through chamba of Himachal Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ravi river.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ravi River, one of the five rivers of Punjab, is a perennial river approximately 720 km long, originating from the Bara Bhangal area in the Himalayas (Kullu hills, Himachal Pradesh) and flowing through the Chamba district of Himachal Pradesh. (रावी नदी — चंबा, हिमाचल प्रदेश)

 

• After flowing through Himachal Pradesh, it enters Punjab and eventually joins the Chenab River in Pakistan.

 

• The Ravi is one of the three Eastern Rivers (along with the Beas and Sutlej) allocated to India under the Indus Waters Treaty (1960).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Chamera Dam, a major hydroelectric project, is built on the Ravi River in Himachal Pradesh.

 

• The historic city of Lahore (Pakistan) is situated on the banks of the Ravi River.

 

NOTE

 

• Saryu river (Option 1): A tributary of the Ghaghara, associated with Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh.

 

• Yamuna river (Option 2): Originates from the Yamunotri Glacier in Uttarakhand; the longest tributary of the Ganga.

 

• Krishna river (Option 4): Originates at Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra, flowing through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh; it is a peninsular (not Himalayan) river.

question: The Rourkela steel plant was set up in collaboration with Germany in which state of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Rourkela Steel Plant, India's first integrated public sector steel plant, is located in Rourkela, Odisha, and was set up in collaboration with West Germany (with the German firms Krupp and Demag). (राउरकेला इस्पात संयंत्र — ओडिशा)

 

• It was established in the 1950s during the Second Five-Year Plan, and commenced production in 1959, under the Rourkela Steel Plant agreement of 1955.

 

• It is managed by the Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhilai Steel Plant (Chhattisgarh) was set up with Soviet Union (USSR) collaboration, and Durgapur Steel Plant (West Bengal) with British collaboration — all three were flagship projects of the Second Five-Year Plan.

 

• Odisha is also home to other major steel and mining hubs, including Rourkela's rich iron ore deposits from the Sundargarh district.

 

NOTE

 

• Jharkhand (Option 1): Home to steel plants like the Tata Steel Plant, Jamshedpur (private sector, oldest steel plant in India) and Bokaro Steel Plant (Soviet collaboration).

 

• Bihar (Option 2) and Assam (Option 3): Neither hosts the Rourkela Steel Plant; both are incorrect.

question: The Governor of an Indian state before entering upon his office takes an oath or affirmation before ________.
option_1: the Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to the State
option_3: the Chief Minister of the concerned state
solution_text:
The correct answer is the Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to the State.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Article 159 of the Constitution of India, the Governor, before entering upon office, must make and subscribe an oath or affirmation before the Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to that State, or in his absence, the senior-most judge of that Court available. (राज्यपाल की शपथ — उच्च न्यायालय के मुख्य न्यायाधीश)

 

• Through this oath, the Governor swears to faithfully execute the office, to preserve, protect and defend the Constitution and the law, and to devote themselves to the service and well-being of the people of the State.

 

• This is distinct from the oath of the President of India, which is administered by the Chief Justice of India (Article 60).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Governor is appointed by the President of India under Article 155 and holds office during the pleasure of the President, as per Article 156.

 

• Articles 153 to 167 in Part VI of the Constitution deal with the State Executive, including the Governor.

 

NOTE

 

• The President of India (Option 2): The President's own oath is administered by the Chief Justice of India, not the Governor's.

 

• The Chief Minister of the concerned state (Option 3): Plays no role in administering the Governor's oath.

 

• The Prime Minister of India (Option 4): Also plays no role in administering the Governor's oath.

question: In 2022, the Government of India urged people to hoist or display the Tricolour in their homes from August ______________to 15th to celebrate Independence Day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 13th.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under the "Har Ghar Tiranga" campaign, launched to mark 75 years of India's independence (Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav), the Government of India urged citizens to hoist or display the Tricolour at their homes from 13 August to 15 August 2022. (हर घर तिरंगा — 13 से 15 अगस्त)

 

• The campaign was launched by the Ministry of Culture under the Azadi Ka Amrit Mahotsav initiative, aimed at invoking a sense of patriotism and promoting awareness about the national flag.

 

• This period also coincided with amendments to the Flag Code of India, 2002, permitting the display of the flag day and night (previously restricted to sunrise to sunset) and allowing machine-made and polyester flags.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Flag Code of India governs the display and use of the National Flag of India; it was last significantly amended in 2021-22 to support the Har Ghar Tiranga campaign.

 

• India's Independence Day, 15 August, marks the day India gained independence from British rule in 1947.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 (12th, 10th, 11th) are incorrect, as the official campaign period was specifically 13 to 15 August 2022.

question: Which of the following combinations of “animal” and “area they found” is INCORRECT?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Orangutan – Caribbean islands.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Orangutan is native to the rainforests of the islands of Borneo and Sumatra in Southeast Asia, not the Caribbean islands, making this combination INCORRECT. (ऑरंगउटान — दक्षिण-पूर्व एशिया)

 

• Kangaroo – Australia is correct: Kangaroos are native marsupials found predominantly in Australia and parts of New Guinea.

 

• Ostrich – Savanna and desert regions is correct: Ostriches are native to the savannas and semi-arid regions of Africa.

 

• Lemurs – Madagascar is correct: Lemurs are primates found almost exclusively on the island of Madagascar and some smaller neighbouring islands.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Orangutans are critically endangered, threatened primarily by deforestation and palm oil plantations in Borneo and Sumatra.

 

• Madagascar's isolation for millions of years has led to a high degree of endemism, with lemurs being its most iconic example.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 3 and 4 (Kangaroo–Australia, Ostrich–Savanna/desert, Lemurs–Madagascar) are correct combinations and hence not the answer, since the question asks for the INCORRECT pair.

question: Who among the following is an exponent of the classical instrument, Santoor?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pandit Shivkumar Sharma.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Shivkumar Sharma was a renowned Indian classical musician, widely credited with popularising the Santoor as a solo classical instrument, elevating it from a folk instrument of Kashmir to the concert stage. (संतूर — पंडित शिवकुमार शर्मा)

 

• The Santoor is a trapezoid-shaped hammered dulcimer with numerous strings, traditionally used in Kashmiri Sufiana music.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan (2001) and collaborated extensively with flautist Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia under the name "Shiv-Hari", including for Bollywood film music.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other legendary Santoor players include Bhajan Sopori and Rahul Sharma (son of Shivkumar Sharma).

 

• Pandit Shivkumar Sharma passed away in May 2022.

 

NOTE

 

• Pandit Kumar Gandharva (Option 1): A renowned Hindustani classical vocalist, known for his unique style blending folk elements.

 

• Pandit Bhimsen Joshi (Option 2): A legendary Hindustani classical vocalist of the Kirana Gharana, recipient of the Bharat Ratna.

 

• Pandit Ravi Shankar (Option 3): A world-renowned sitar maestro, recipient of the Bharat Ratna, father of Anoushka Shankar and Norah Jones.

question:
The given equation provides the property of the motion of an object, traversing a circular path. What is ‘v’ in this equation?

ac = v2/R
solution_text:
The correct answer is Speed.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The equation ac = v²/R represents the formula for centripetal acceleration, where ac is the centripetal acceleration, v is the (linear/tangential) speed of the object, and R is the radius of the circular path. (अभिकेंद्रीय त्वरण — चाल)

 

• Centripetal acceleration is the acceleration directed towards the centre of the circular path, responsible for continuously changing the direction of the object's velocity so that it moves in a circle.

 

• The corresponding centripetal force is given by F = mv²/R, where m is the mass of the object.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Centripetal acceleration can also be expressed as ac = ω²R, where ω is the angular velocity.

 

• Real-world examples of centripetal force include the tension in a string when swinging a stone, and gravitational force providing the centripetal force for planetary orbits.

 

NOTE

 

• Distance (Option 1), Surface area (Option 2) and Intensity (Option 4) are incorrect as none of these physical quantities appear as 'v' in the centripetal acceleration formula — 'v' specifically denotes speed.

question: In hockey, ________ is awarded if the ball goes over the back line after last being touched by a defender.
solution_text:
The correct answer is long corner.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In field hockey, a long corner is awarded to the attacking team when the ball unintentionally crosses the back line (end line), other than the goal-line, after last being touched by a defender. (हॉकी — लॉन्ग कॉर्नर)

 

• It is restarted with a hit taken from a mark 5 metres from the nearest corner flag, along the side-line or back-line.

 

• If a defender plays the ball over the back line intentionally, or commits certain fouls inside the shooting circle, the umpire instead awards a penalty corner, a more advantageous restart for the attacking team.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• A penalty corner is awarded for intentional fouls by defenders inside the circle, or for intentionally playing the ball over the back-line, and gives the attacking side a strong scoring opportunity.

 

• A free hit is awarded for most other fouls occurring outside the shooting circle.

 

NOTE

 

• Off side (Option 2): The offside rule has actually been abolished in modern field hockey (removed in 1998); it is not the correct restart here in any case.

 

• Free hit (Option 3): Awarded for general fouls, not specifically for the ball crossing the back line off a defender.

 

• Penalty corner (Option 4): Awarded for intentional fouls/offences by defenders in the circle, not for an ordinary/unintentional deflection over the back-line.

question: The Social Justice and Empowerment Ministry of India, which caters to the welfare of the backward classes and those with disabilities, saw _______ increase in the allocation in the Union Budget 2022-23.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 12%.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the Union Budget 2022-23, the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, which looks after the welfare of backward classes and persons with disabilities, saw a 12% increase in its budgetary allocation, receiving approximately ₹13,134 crore. (सामाजिक न्याय मंत्रालय बजट — 12% वृद्धि)

 

• The Union Budget 2022-23 was presented by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on 1 February 2022.

 

• The increased allocation was aimed at strengthening schemes for scheduled castes, other backward classes, senior citizens and persons with disabilities (Divyangjan).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Key schemes under this ministry include the Post-Matric Scholarship Scheme for SCs, PM-DAKSH, and the Accessible India Campaign (Sugamya Bharat Abhiyan).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 (15%, 5%, 10%) are incorrect as the actual increase recorded in Budget 2022-23 for this ministry was 12%.

question: The term of trade refers to ________.
option_1: the excess of import expenditures over export earnings
option_3: the terms and conditions on which a country is offered loan
option_4: the ratio between export prices and import prices
solution_text:
The correct answer is the ratio between export prices and import prices.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Terms of Trade (ToT) refers to the ratio between a country's export prices and its import prices, indicating the relative value of exports in terms of imports. (व्यापार की शर्तें — निर्यात-आयात मूल्य अनुपात)

 

• It is typically expressed as: ToT = (Index of Export Prices / Index of Import Prices) × 100.

 

• A rise in the terms of trade (favourable ToT) means a country can import more goods for a given quantity of exports; a fall (unfavourable ToT) means the opposite.

 

• Terms of trade is a key indicator used in international economics to assess a country's trading position and economic welfare from trade.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• A country's Balance of Trade (BoT) refers to the difference between the value of its exports and imports, which is distinct from terms of trade.

 

• Developing/primary-good-exporting countries often face declining/unfavourable terms of trade relative to manufactured-goods exporters, a concept central to the Prebisch-Singer hypothesis.

 

NOTE

 

• The excess of import expenditures over export earnings (Option 1): This describes a trade deficit, not the terms of trade.

 

• The trade agreements (Option 2): This refers to formal agreements between countries governing trade, unrelated to the terms of trade concept.

 

• The terms and conditions on which a country is offered loan (Option 3): This pertains to loan/credit conditions, not terms of trade.

question: ________of the Constitution of India says that the State shall take steps to organise panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 40.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 40 of the Constitution of India, under Part IV (Directive Principles of State Policy), directs the State to "take steps to organise village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government". (अनुच्छेद 40 — पंचायत)

 

• This Gandhian principle inspired the eventual establishment of the three-tier Panchayati Raj system in India.

 

• The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 gave concrete constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions by adding Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule to the Constitution, operationalising the spirit of Article 40.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 73rd Amendment came into force on 24 April 1993, which is now celebrated as National Panchayati Raj Day.

 

• The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 similarly established urban local bodies (Municipalities) through Part IXA and the Twelfth Schedule.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 35 (Option 1): Deals with legislation to give effect to certain Fundamental Rights (Part III).

 

• Article 38 (Option 3): Directs the State to promote the welfare of the people by securing a social order with social, economic and political justice.

 

• Article 32 (Option 4): Provides the Right to Constitutional Remedies, allowing citizens to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights; famously called the "heart and soul" of the Constitution by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar.

question: Which of the following is a Disability Screening Mobile App developed by NCERT launched in Delhi schools to screen students with suspected disabilities?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PRASHAST.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• PRASHAST (Screening Tool and Guidelines for Screening of Children with Disabilities) is a mobile app developed by the NCERT (National Council of Educational Research and Training), used in Delhi and other schools to screen students with suspected disabilities. (प्रशस्त ऐप — एनसीईआरटी)

 

• The app helps teachers identify children who may have specific learning disabilities, sensory impairments, or other disabilities at an early stage, supporting timely intervention.

 

• It was developed in line with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD) Act, 2016, and the Samagra Shiksha scheme's focus on inclusive education.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Samagra Shiksha is the Government of India's umbrella programme for school education, covering pre-school to Class 12, integrating erstwhile schemes like SSA, RMSA and Teacher Education.

 

• NCERT is an autonomous organisation set up in 1961 that develops the national curriculum framework and school textbooks (NCERT textbooks) in India.

 

NOTE

 

• SAMAGRA (Option 1): Refers to "Samagra Shiksha", the umbrella school education scheme, not a disability screening app.

 

• VIDYAN (Option 2) and SAMAGAM (Option 4): Not recognised NCERT disability-screening mobile apps; they do not correspond to any such official tool.
